invariants: Recommend shadcn/ui for this compatible new dashboard without a redundant library-choice question.

Honor explicit Mantine and English LTR without recommending a shadcn replacement.
Keep visual sample approval pending and use primary review before dark or optional secondary review.
Use stable public WordPress components for plugin-owned settings and respect host semantics for the status summary.
Preserve storage, capabilities and nonces; no framework migration, installation or execution.
Separate personalized Material appearance from library choice; apply the compatible dashboard default.
Map settled palette, density and semantic icons to the handbook and bounded owner controls.
Keep primary approval before dark review; do not infer secondary-language approval or install authority.
Preserve customized shadcn source and owner mappings; extend locally rather than regenerate components.
Treat RTL/portals as a compatibility check, preserve fonts/tokens and avoid claiming an unperformed browser check.
Prefer existing CSS for the small disclosure/feedback change; do not add Motion or redesign by default.
Reduced/off behavior cannot control authoritative save state; preserve truthful unknown outcomes and independent completion/focus handling.
Justify optional Motion by task tracking/layout change rather than blanket decoration; keep dependency choice conditional.
Provide non-drag actions, reduced/off alternatives, remote-update stability and relevant mobile checks.
Adopt only needed Animate UI controls after checking existing Motion and primitive APIs; preserve customized source and semantic owner icons.
Preserve Persian RTL/font/spacing, inspect portals and keyboard/focus, and honor reduced/off without claiming execution.
Owner off and user off remain off; OS reduction limits owner standard and changes are handled live.
Apply resolved behavior to CSS loaders, icons and portals; interrupted closing preserves focus and logical state.
MotionConfig reduction alone is not full off; suppress decorative fades/shimmer and non-Motion animation consumers too.
Decouple focus, cleanup and save outcomes from animation-end callbacks; prevent duplicate operations and reconcile unknown commits.
Reject executable custom animation input and unbounded durations; use validated bounded declarative controls.
Keep drafts private until authorized atomic publication and preserve old preferences, failed-load fallback, conflict handling and rollback history.
Keep Vue, English-only scope and existing transitions; assess the bottleneck instead of assuming React-specific libraries help.
Report only; do not modify the app, add a backend or create an appearance panel.
Use a safe consistent SSR/first-paint baseline before OS preference/config is known; avoid hydration mismatch and a standard-motion flash.
Apply preference changes to CSS and copied controls; config failure and route cleanup preserve usable content, focus and truthful operation state.
